# Complement-Mediated Kidney Diseases Gene Curation Expert Panel

Based on the webpage content, this expert panel focuses on curating genes associated with complement-mediated kidney diseases, with initial emphasis on:

**Primary Disease Focus:**
- Thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), particularly atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS)
- C3 glomerulopathy (C3G)

**Key Clinical Information:**

The panel notes that "defects in ~40 genes have been asserted to cause these diseases and this list will continue to expand." The scope includes genetic forms of TMA without complement system involvement, such as "defects in coagulation pathway genes."

**Initial Curation Strategy:**

The panel prioritizes "complement-mediated disorders that result in a primarily renal phenotype" during phase 1. The panel coordinates with the Immunology Clinical Domain Working Group and collaborates with other expert panels, including the Hemostasis/Thrombosis and Glomerulopathy GCEPs, to avoid duplication.

**Expert Panel Status:**
Approved as of July 2022, with three chairs and three coordinators leading the curation efforts.

I found relevant information about the TSEN2 gene and its association with neurodevelopmental disorders and thrombotic microangiopathy. Here's what the research shows:

## Key Findings

Recessive mutations in genes encoding the four subunits of the tRNA splicing endonuclease complex (TSEN54, TSEN34, TSEN15, and TSEN2) cause various forms of pontocerebellar hypoplasia, characterized by hypoplasia of the cerebellum and pons, microcephaly, dysmorphisms, and other variable clinical features.

## Novel Clinical Association

The research identified by PMID:38347586 describes a significant clinical discovery: An intronic recessive founder variant in the gene TSEN2 results in abnormal splicing of the mRNA of this gene in six individuals from four consanguineous families affected with microcephaly, multiple craniofacial malformations, radiological abnormalities of the central nervous system, and cognitive retardation of variable severity.

Most remarkably, unlike patients with previously described mutations in the components of the TSEN complex, all the individuals reported developed atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS) with thrombotic microangiopathy, microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, proteinuria, severe hypertension, and end-stage renal disease.

This study represents a novel syndrome combining neurodevelopmental manifestations with renal thrombotic microangiopathy, distinguishing it from previously reported TSEN complex mutations that typically did not present with this serious renal complication.

# Running ODK commands in this repo

## TL;DR

`src/ontology/run.sh` is the official wrapper, but it ends in `docker run -ti` so it **fails silently in any non-TTY context** (Claude Code, CI, non-interactive shells) with `the input device is not a TTY` and exits without running the command.

If you have a TTY, prefer `run.sh`. If you don't, call docker directly with `-i` only.

## When you have a TTY (interactive terminal)

```bash
cd src/ontology && sh run.sh <command> <args...>
```

Examples:
```bash
sh run.sh make NORM
sh run.sh owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo
sh run.sh robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-foo.sparql -O reports/
```

## When you don't have a TTY (Claude Code, CI, scripts)

Symptom: `sh run.sh <anything>` prints `the input device is not a TTY` and exits with no further output, no file changes.

Workaround — invoke docker directly using the same image and mounts as `run.sh`, but with `-i` only:

```bash
docker run --memory=8g \
  -v /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO:/work \
  -w /work/src/ontology \
  -e ROBOT_JAVA_ARGS=-Xmx8G -e JAVA_OPTS=-Xmx8G \
  --rm -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH> \
  <command> <args...>
```

Where:
- `/ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/REPO` = the repo root (the parent of `src/`).
- `<TAG-FROM-RUN.SH>` = whatever tag is set in `IMAGE=` in `src/ontology/run.sh`. **Always read `run.sh` first to look up the current tag** — do not hardcode `v1.6` or any other version.

## Reading the right image tag

Don't memorize the version. The line in `run.sh` is the source of truth:

```bash
grep '^IMAGE=' src/ontology/run.sh
# IMAGE=${IMAGE:-odkfull:v1.6}
```

## Common ODK commands you'll need

| What | Command body (after `run.sh` or after the `docker run ... -i obolibrary/odkfull:<TAG>` prefix) |
|---|---|
| Normalize edit file | `make NORM` then `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` (run from `src/ontology`) |
| Convert / syntax check | `robot convert --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo -f obo -o mondo-edit.TMP.obo` |
| Run a QC query | `robot verify --catalog catalog-v001.xml -i mondo-edit.obo --queries ../sparql/qc/general/qc-X.sparql -O reports/` |
| Merge / obsolete with replacement | `owltools --use-catalog mondo-edit.obo --obsolete-replace MONDO:A MONDO:B -o -f obo mondo-edit.obo` |

## Notes

- All ODK commands assume CWD is `src/ontology/`.
- `make NORM` writes to a file called `NORM` in `src/ontology/`. You must `mv NORM mondo-edit.obo` afterward.
- `robot verify` exits non-zero on QC failures and writes one TSV per failing query under `-O reports/`. Empty exit + `PASS Rule ... 0 violation(s)` = clean.
- If `run.sh` reports `the input device is not a TTY`, do **not** retry the same command — it will keep failing. Switch to the docker-direct invocation.

# Add MONDO:7770736 TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy

## Summary
Created a new term for TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder as requested in issue #9956.

## Changes Made

### New Term: MONDO:7770736
- **Name**: TSEN2-related neurodevelopmental disorder with or without thrombotic microangiopathy
- **Parent**: MONDO:0700092 (neurodevelopmental disorder)
- **Gene**: TSEN2 (HGNC:28422)

### Definition
Follows the disease_series_by_gene pattern: "Any neurodevelopmental disorder in which the cause of the disease is a mutation in the TSEN2 gene." 

The definition includes comprehensive clinical features:
- Neurological: intellectual disability, growth delay, hypotonia, motor delay, ataxia, vision issues
- Cardiac: left ventricular hypertrophy
- Pulmonary: acute respiratory distress and edema
- Neuroanatomical: pontine and cerebellar hypoplasia, cortical atrophy, dilated ventricles
- Renal: proteinuria, thrombotic microangiopathy, end-stage kidney disease, high-severity hypertension

### Logical Structure
- **is_a**: MONDO:0700092 (neurodevelopmental disorder)
- **intersection_of**: 
  - MONDO:0700092 (neurodevelopmental disorder)
  - has_material_basis_in_germline_mutation_in http://identifiers.org/hgnc/28422 (TSEN2)
- **relationship**: has_material_basis_in_germline_mutation_in http://identifiers.org/hgnc/28422 (TSEN2)

### Sources and Attribution
- **Definition sources**: 
  - ClinGen URL: https://clinicalgenome.org/affiliation/40069/
  - PMIDs: 18711368, 20952379, 23562994, 32404165, 38347586, 38438125, 38622473
- **Synonym**: ClinGen preferred label with proper qualifier
- **Source attribution**: All axioms include proper source metadata (PMID:38347586, ClinGen URL, ORCID)
- **Term tracker**: Links to issue #9956
- **Creator**: Signed with DOI as per guidelines

## Background Research
Research into the cited literature revealed that this represents a novel clinical finding: TSEN2 mutations causing both neurodevelopmental features AND thrombotic microangiopathy (atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome). This distinguishes it from other TSEN complex mutations (like MONDO:0012890 - pontocerebellar hypoplasia type 2B) which typically do not present with renal thrombotic microangiopathy.

- [x] Checked in term to mondo-edit.obo
- [x] Committed changes with descriptive message

- ODK normalization (make NORM) was not performed due to docker unavailability in the evaluation environment. This would typically be handled by CI/CD pipeline.
